rationale: There is emerging evidence supporting earlier seizure onset and a higher prevalence of epileptic spasms/tonic seizures in biallelic RNU2-2 cases compared to dominant de novo cases, but major cohort studies diverge on the degree of phenotypic distinctness and exact onset timing. Henry et al. (2026) report a median onset of 10.5 months in biallelic DEE with predominant infantile spasms and tonic seizures transitioning to Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, contrasting with 21–24 months in dominant cases. Jackson et al. (2026) report seizure onset during the first year of life in 61.8% of recessive cases. However, Leitão et al. (2026) in the largest cohort study (91 biallelic individuals from 73 families) report a later median onset of 1.5 years (18 months) with a wide range spanning 8 weeks to 16 years, and emphasize broad clinical phenotypic overlap and a continuous 'gradient-of-impact model bridging dominant and recessive inheritance' rather than a clear-cut dichotomy.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 14 individuals with biallelic RNU2-2 variants clustering in the 5' conserved domains, all presented with severe DEE. Infantile spasms and tonic seizures were predominant, progression to Lennox-Gastaut syndrome was common, and median seizure onset was 10.5 months compared to 21 months in dominant cases.

conflicts: Henry et al. (2026) report an infantile median onset age of 10.5 months in biallelic cases with predominant infantile spasms/tonic seizures and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome-like presentation, whereas Leitão et al. (2026) report a higher median onset of 1.5 years (18 months) with onset extending up to 16 years.

Jackson et al. (2026) state that the recessive RNU2-2 condition is clinically and mechanistically distinct from the dominant disorder, whereas Leitão et al. (2026) conclude that dominant and recessive forms share extensive phenotypic overlap and represent a biological gradient of impact across noncoding snRNA variants.

new_directions.question_text: Does direct head-to-head comparison of standardized semiology (epileptic spasms, tonic seizures, myoclonic seizures) between age-matched dominant and recessive RNU2-2 cohorts demonstrate statistically significant separation?
new_directions.rationale: Current cohorts differ in ascertainment (epilepsy genetics clinics versus general rare disease cohorts), confounding apparent differences in seizure onset age and predominant semiologies.

new_directions.question_text: Do specific 5' snRNA domain variant configurations dictate early-infantile spasm presentation versus later childhood DEE within biallelic RNU2-2 patients?
new_directions.rationale: Biallelic cases exhibit broad variation in onset (8 weeks to 16 years); determining whether structural disruption of U2-2 snRNA core base-pairing correlates with infantile spasm onset would explain cohort discordance.
